To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the yeast WASP Las17 has a second G‐Actin‐binding motif that functions in Arp2‐3 complex‐mediated actino assembly and endocytosis.
a second G‐Actin‐binding motif of Las17 (LGM) is necessary for normal actin polymerization and endocytosis in vivo.
Las17 contains two G‐actin binding motifs, one of which is required for normal actin assembly during endocytosis in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanism of actomyosin‐based cell motility.
the mechanism by which the Arp2‐3 complex, a highly conserved actin‐nucleating complex that is required for actin‐based motility, is activated during endocytosis.
the molecular mechanism of actin‐based force generation during endocytosis and the identification of new actin‐binding motifs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WH2 motif is the major actin‐binding site of the Las17 protein, while the LGM is the second, weaker actin‐binding motif.
LGM is necessary but not sufficient for normal Arp 2/3‐ mediated actin assembly during clathrin‐ mediated endocytosis.
LGM is necessary but not sufficient for normal actin dynamics during CME, and its function is dependent on the WH2 motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Las17 G‐binding motif LGM is necessary but insufficient for optimal actin polymerization and CME.
Las17 contains two G‐actin binding motifs that cooperate to stimulate actin assembly in vivo.
the Las17 LGM motif binds G‐actins and is necessary for optimal actin polymerization, which in turn is necessary for normal endocytosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the yeast endocytic protein Las17 has a second globular actin‐binding motif that is necessary and sufficient for Arp2/ 3‐mediated branched actin assembly in vitro.
Las17 has two G‐actin binding motifs that function in concert to promote actin assembly during yeast endocytosis.
Las17 has two distinct G‐actin binding motifs, WH2 and LGM, that have different affinities and potencies.
